neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were all from the same family, had a dispute with the victim's family due to the victim's son teasing the daughter of one of the accused. The accused gathered in a house, consumed liquor, and then came out into the street with weapons, raising a lalkara (threatening retribution). They attacked the victim and his brother, causing injuries. The victim's brother succumbed to his injuries. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts and medical evidence, including a post-mortem report. The accused claimed the dispute arose from election rivalries and some had alibis. The trial court acquitted some accused and convicted others for the murder of the victim's brother. The High Court affirmed the trial court's decision.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the injury caused to the deceased was directly and deeply inflicted into the stomach, a vital part, leading to death within a short time, and that the accused had a common intention to cause that injury.

quotes.text: In the case before us, we find that a lalkara had been raised by the accused threatening retribution on account of the misbehaviour of Darshan Singh, son of Sher Singh with Nindo a few days earlier and that the accused had been drinking together in the house of Parshottarn Singh and had thereafter come out leading to the incident.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that even if the prosecution's case was true, the matter would not fall under murder but under culpable homicide not amounting to murder. They also claimed that the injury attributed to Sher Singh could have resulted from a scuffle and not from a lathi, and that the provisions of Section 34 of the IPC were not made out as there was no intention to commit murder.

quotes.text: It has also been submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the provisions of Section 34 of the IPC were not made out as there was no intention on the part of the accused to commit murder.

It has finally been submitted that Sher Singh accused, appellant was similarly situated as those acquitted by the trial court as the injury attributed to him on the shoulder of Rajwinder Singh could have caused as a result of a scuffle during the incident and was not possible with a lathi.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the question of whether the injury was caused with the intention to cause death is a matter of objective satisfaction of the Court, based on the facts and circumstances of the case.

quotes.text: It is true that clause thirdly of Section 300 of the IPC deals with a case where the intention was to cause the very injury found on the dead body.

We are, therefore, of the opinion, that the injury in the present case had been caused directly and deep into the stomach of the deceased, a very vital part, which had led to death within a short time.
